about: Source for course/<module>/README.md and hub-map.json. Edit this, then run python3 tools/build_course.py. Process maps and hours come from APG audits of real businesses, anonymised; hours are staff estimates.

modules.name: Lead generation
modules.who: Owner, or a sales rep in the bigger ones
modules.promise: Know where your next jobs are coming from, without the Sunday-night spreadsheet.

steps.what: Tender portals, builders you know, Google, word of mouth
Size, location, who's building it
Look up the estimator or PM, find a number
Type the lead into the CRM or a spreadsheet
Calls, capability statement, ask to be on the tender list
Check in until the job comes up

time_goes: Follow-ups run weeks late, so the job's specified before anyone rings
10 h a week calling and 8 h a week updating the CRM, for one rep
Contacts can't be sorted by area or type, so every email goes to everyone
Tender alert emails pile up unread

intake.what: Map where your work comes from: the sources, who chases them, and what gets written down.

skills.name: Tender watch
skills.what: A morning list of new tenders and who's building them, from your portal emails

skills.name: Follow-up list
skills.what: Who to ring this week and why, with the message drafted

skills.name: Contact tidy-up
skills.what: Sorts your contacts by area and type so a campaign hits the right people

modules.name: Sales and follow-up
modules.who: Owner or sales rep, office admin
modules.promise: Every enquiry answered and every quote followed up, without retyping it all.

steps.what: Phone, email, website form
Work out which emails are real enquiries
Budget, timing, who decides
Call notes typed or dictated into the CRM
Send the quote, chase it, answer questions
Fill in the handover form for the office or crew

time_goes: Sorting the inbox: 1.5 to 2 h a day per salesperson
Copying emails into the CRM: 20 to 40 min a day per person
Follow-up emails written the next morning, called the most time-consuming part of the job
A 20-question handover typed from the CRM into an email

intake.what: Map how an enquiry becomes a won job: who answers, where notes go, and when you follow up.

skills.name: Inbox sorter
skills.what: Flags the real enquiries and drafts the first reply

skills.name: Call note to CRM
skills.what: Speak after the call: note, task and follow-up email drafted

skills.name: Handover pack
skills.what: The won job's handover questions filled from the quote and emails

modules.name: Quoting, estimating and proposals
modules.who: Owner or estimator, admin types it up
modules.promise: A priced quote on your own rates in minutes, from site or the office.

steps.what: Email, plans, a site visit, photos
Chase anything missing before pricing
On site or from drawings (module 4)
Rates, materials, supplier prices, labour
Typed into a template or the job system
PDF out, logged with a reminder

time_goes: 6 in 10 enquiries go back for missing information before they can be priced
Matching products takes 1 to 2 h on a complex quote; the whole quote 3 to 4 h
The same job written out three times: site notes, Excel, then Word
Rebuilding quotes after site visits: about 13 h a week across one team

intake.what: Walk through your last two quotes: where each number came from, and every step you did by hand.

skills.name: Quote builder
skills.what: Voice note and photos in, a quote on your prices out. Built and live for clients

skills.name: Missing-info check
skills.what: Reads the enquiry and drafts the questions before you price

skills.name: Sheet to skill
skills.what: Drop in the spreadsheet you quote from; it becomes the plugin's questions

modules.name: Takeoffs from drawings
modules.who: Estimator, or the owner at night
modules.promise: Counts and measurements off the plans, marked up and checked, without tracing every line.

steps.what: A pack of 10 to 100+ sheets, by email or a portal
The ones your trade actually needs
Check it against a known dimension
Trace, click, count, by hand
Quantities typed across
New drawings: do it again and compare

time_goes: Takeoff is about 60% of estimating time; data entry another 30%
Big packages: two people for three weeks
Every revision means redoing the takeoff and comparing by eye
After the win, the job team does its own takeoff again

intake.what: Map how you take off: which drawings, what you count, the scale, and where the numbers go.

skills.name: Picture takeoff
skills.what: Reads the plan like a person: counts, measures, marks it up. Built for clients

skills.name: Drawing finder
skills.what: Finds the sheets you need in a 100-drawing pack

skills.name: Revision compare
skills.what: What changed between the tender and construction drawings

lessons.title: Watch it read a drawing
What you get, and what you need to start
Install it and set up your symbol key
Your first drawing: counts and markup
Check it against the drawing's own schedule
Multi-sheet jobs
Push the counts into costing and quoting
7-day check-in: post your first takeoff

modules.name: Purchasing and suppliers
modules.who: Owner, office admin or a purchaser
modules.promise: Supplier quotes turned into checked orders, and price lists kept current.

steps.what: From a won job or the crew
Send the list to two or three suppliers
Line by line, gaps and substitutes
Every line copied into the system
Check the confirmation, chase back-orders
Match to the order and delivery docket (module 10)

time_goes: Copying a supplier quote into an order: 15 to 30 min each, about 15 h a week
Reviewing each supplier quote line by line: 45 to 60 min
Chasing the missing job code: about 3 h a week
Supplier price lists arrive as PDFs and go stale

intake.what: Map how you buy: who orders, which suppliers, how you compare, and where the order is typed.

skills.name: Quote to order
skills.what: Reads the supplier quote, matches job and items, asks instead of guessing

skills.name: Three-supplier compare
skills.what: Side by side, with gaps and substitutes flagged

skills.name: Price list update
skills.what: A supplier's PDF turned into your updated price list

modules.name: Customer service and orders
modules.promise: Orders entered and questions answered fast, by whoever picks up.

steps.what: Shared inbox, phone, a form
Sort and forward to the right person
Line by line from the PDF
Ask around for the product or job answer
Order confirmed, delays passed on

time_goes: A two to three page order: 10 to 30 min to key in
A third of the team's time on enquiries and email
Answers hunted across six places
Shared inboxes forwarded by hand: about 5 h a week

intake.what: Map how a customer message gets handled: where it lands, who picks it up, how orders are entered and where the answers live.

skills.name: Order reader
skills.what: Reads the order PDF and lines it up against your price list

skills.name: Product answers
skills.what: One place to ask, showing where each answer came from

skills.name: Where's my order
skills.what: Status replies drafted from the job system

modules.name: Finance, timesheets and admin
modules.promise: Bills checked, debtors chased and payroll right, without the Friday scramble.

steps.what: Match to the order and delivery docket
Approved, paid, filed (often three places)
Hours in, checked, approved
Checked employee by employee
Invoices out, debtors chased by phone
The report pulled together by hand

time_goes: Each bill saved in three places: about 4 h a week
Chasing debtors: about 12 h a week for one bookkeeper
New starters set up in three systems: about 2 h each
Receipts only on one phone, so the books stop when it's away

intake.what: Map your office week: bills, timesheets, payroll, invoicing, chasing, and who does each.

skills.name: Bill checker
skills.what: Bill against order and docket; only the mismatches come to you

skills.name: Debtor chase list
skills.what: Who to chase today, emails drafted

skills.name: Payroll check
skills.what: Hours against pay, exceptions only. Being built

modules.name: Job delivery and scheduling
modules.promise: From won job to handover with the paperwork keeping up, not the other way round.

steps.what: Job in the system, folders, the handover
Dates, crew and subbies, client told
SWMS, inductions, compliance checks
Progress, photos and issues in group chats
Weekly client report, variations, progress claim
Defects, photos, close-out (module 9)

time_goes: Project managers spend up to 80% of their week on admin
Site updates in WhatsApp turned into data by hand: about 10 h a week per person
A weekly client report: about 3.5 h per active job
A progress claim: half a day to a day per job per month

intake.what: Map a job from won to handed over: who sets it up, how the crew is booked, and what gets reported.

skills.what: Folders, job and checklist made from the won quote

skills.name: Site update to report

modules.name: Stock, warehouse and freight
modules.who: Warehouse lead, logistics or office admin
modules.promise: Know what's in stock, what's going out, and what freight really costs you.

steps.what: Check against the docket, put away
Picked from the list, checked
Sizes and weights, carrier portal or email
Which truck, which day
Carrier booked, dockets printed
Proof of delivery, freight invoice checked

time_goes: A freight quote waits on the one person who knows the packed sizes, six times a day
Freight sheet re-edited every time dates move: about 4 h a week
The same loads retyped into the carrier email: about 3 h a week
Waiting-time charges found on the invoice and never passed on

intake.what: Map how stock comes in and goes out: who books freight, how loads are planned, where it's recorded.

skills.what: Sizes from the order, carrier request drafted

skills.name: Load planner
skills.what: This week's deliveries grouped into loads by site and date

skills.name: Delivery charges log
skills.what: Waiting time and failed trips logged so they can be charged on

modules.name: After-sales, warranty and maintenance
modules.promise: Every callback starts with the full history, and the close-out writes itself.

steps.what: Email, phone, a ticket
What was supplied, past visits, the drawings

steps.step: Decide: fix by phone or visit
steps.what: Most visits are booked without the history
Photos, notes, a report written up later
Report sent, invoice, warranty or credit
Service contracts, asset lists, renewals

time_goes: Every callback treated as new; repeat faults go unseen
In one business, two of three trips in a week could have been avoided
Close-out paperwork: about 5 h a week, more work than the repair
Maintenance contracts and renewals: about 26 h a week for one person

intake.what: Map what happens after the job: how callbacks come in, what history you check, how you close out.

skills.name: Site history
skills.what: Everything supplied and every past visit, before anyone goes

skills.name: Spoken close-out
skills.what: One voice debrief becomes the report, photos and invoice notes

skills.name: Renewal builder
skills.what: Last year's contract and asset list turned into this year's
